title: Long-Term Savings: Your Anchor for Financial Security in Old Age
description: India's Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) has highlighted the critical need for individuals to prioritise long-term pension investments over short-term trading. Pe.

faq.q: What is the National Pension System (NPS)?
faq.a: NPS is a voluntary, long-term retirement savings scheme regulated by PFRDA, allowing individuals to save for retirement through market-linked investments. It offers flexibility in asset allocation and fund managers.

faq.q: How does EPF differ from NPS?
faq.a: EPF is a mandatory, employer-backed provident fund for salaried employees with fixed contributions and guaranteed interest rates. NPS is voluntary, open to all citizens, and offers market-linked returns with investment choices.

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) invest in NPS?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs can open an NPS account. They can contribute to NPS from their NRE/NRO accounts, and the accumulated corpus is repatriable as per FEMA guidelines.

faq.q: What are the main tax benefits of investing in pension schemes?
faq.a: Contributions to EPF and PPF are deductible under Section 80C (up to ₹1.5 lakhs). NPS offers additional deductions under Section 80CCD(1B) (up to ₹50,000) and for employer contributions under Section 80CCD(2).

faq.q: Is it too late to start investing in a pension plan if I'm in my 40s?
faq.a: No, it's never too late to start. While starting early maximises compounding, even starting in your 40s can significantly boost your retirement corpus, especially by making consistent and higher contributions.

faq.q: What happens to my NPS corpus upon retirement?
faq.a: Upon retirement (typically at age 60), you can withdraw up to 60% of your NPS corpus as a tax-free lump sum. The remaining 40% must be used to purchase an annuity plan from an IRDAI-regulated life insurance company, providing a regular pension. [cite: 8, irdai.gov.in]

based_on.title: ‘Less exciting long-term savings crucial for financial security in old age’: CEA encourages pension investment

fact_check.summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of long-term savings and pension schemes in India, with most factual claims verified by authoritative sources.

corrections.note: Corrected the limits for employer contributions to NPS under Section 80CCD(2) based on verified information from income tax and pension regulatory sources.

edits.why: The original claim incorrectly stated that the employer's contribution to NPS under Section 80CCD(2) was without any monetary limit. Authoritative sources clarify that the deduction is limited to 10% of salary for private sector employees and 14% for government employees, with an overall annual ceiling of ₹7.5 lakh for combined employer contributions to NPS, EPF, and Superannuation funds.
